0.original: <hex:024804F201FC03><hex:024904F201FD03> Quest Sync<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103><hex:02100103>A remorseful Tonatiuh wishes to apologize.

1.original: Deeply sorry for having inadvertently devoured the porxie familiar, Tonatiuh decides to return to Wolekdorf with you to apologize.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Please note that the difficulty of this quest has been synced to your current level.

2.original: Though the aggrieved Nu Mou praises Tonatiuh for having the courage to admit his mistake, they nonetheless demand fitting reparation of him: his life. The high price comes as a shock to all, but Tonatiuh earns a concession by choosing to join the Wolekdorf flock. If he can but bring the Nu Mou a bottle of pristine water, a lump of fine clay, and a fae lamp, his debt will be considered settled. Breathing a sigh of relief, you turn to the young amaro to discuss the task of procuring the items.

3.original: While Tonatiuh goes about obtaining the clay, you are tasked with drawing the water. At Sandman's suggestion, you strike out northwest in search of a stream fed by a cascade.

4.original: You find the stream and draw a bottle of pristine water, which you stow in your borrowed sack. Your task accomplished, you set out for the fields of Voeburtenburg to rejoin Tonatiuh.

5.original: Tonatiuh happily reports that he has the clay. All that remains to be obtained, then, is the fae lamp.

26.original: Draw a bottle of pristine water.

27.original: Deliver the pristine water to Tonatiuh.

48.original: Every one of ours claims to have no knowledge of the porxie. That leaves us with only Tonatiuh. Please hurry and find him.

49.original: It was in Voeburtenburg that my poor porxie was devoured. Go on and bring back this Tonatiuh, and we will have the truth!

50.original: So soon after I refuse the offer to live in Wolekdorf, I'm going there to apologize...

51.original: <sigh> Well, there's no use delaying it. Let's be on our way.

52.original: Judging by their dark expression, I take it that's the porxie's master...

53.original: So, you were right. It was an amaro from outside Il Mheg. Very well, I will claim reparation from this Tonatiuh.

54.original: My thanks for bringing back Tonatiuh. Now we shall be able to clear up the misunderstanding.

55.original: I'm so sorry I ate your pig. It's just...I was dreadfully hungry, and it looked so delicious...

56.original: Porxies are not pigs, I'll have you know. They are our people's favored familiars. We treat them as we would our family.

57.original: Now, I praise you for having the courage to admit your mistake. However, I cannot let this grievance stand without fitting reparation. Such is the way of we Nu Mou.

58.original: I understand. What would you have of me?

59.original: Hmmm... Were you a denizen of Wolekdorf, I would take into account the good relations between our peoples and give you a concession.

60.original: But seeing as you are not, I have no choice but to demand full payment: a life for a life.

61.original: A-A life? You mean...I have to die!?

62.original: I want to take responsibility for my actions...but I'm afraid to die. What should I do?

64.original: You can join the Wolekdorf flock.

65.original: I'm afraid there's no other way.

66.original: Ah, indeed! If Tonatiuh were to become one of us, he would be afforded a concession. How does that sound, young one?

67.original: Surely there is something we can do. As our Nu Mou friend says, a denizen of Wolekdorf would be afforded a concession.

68.original: If Tonatiuh were to join our flock, he need not render up his life. How does that sound, young one?

69.original: But...I've already refused your invitation, and since then I've caused only trouble. In spite of all this, you would still let me join you?

70.original: Come now, to be a flock is to look after one another. And there will be times, I'm sure, when you help your fellows as we help you now.

71.original: Besides, such things are of no consequence beside the joy of welcoming a new member to the flock.

72.original: Then it's decided. I will hereby demand reparation of Tonatiuh─as a denizen of Wolekdorf.

73.original: Bring me these three items: a bottle of pristine water, a lump of fine clay, and a fae lamp. By this I will hold the debt settled.

74.original: They might prove challenging for an amaro alone to procure, but then you have a capable mortal here to assist.

76.original: I suppose I've already come this far...

78.original: I'm so sorry for dragging you into this. When all is said and done, I promise to repay your kindness.

79.original: So, that's a bottle of pristine water, a lump of fine clay, and a fae lamp. Please help Tonatiuh gather these things.

80.original: Now that Tonatiuh is a denizen of Wolekdorf, the three items I requested shall suffice by way of reparation.

81.original: Hmmm, being new to Il Mheg, I'm not sure where to begin searching for the items...

82.original: The finest clay may be had from a nearby cliff face. Difficult to reach for men, but an amaro could easily fly there.

83.original: Oh, then I'll go and obtain the clay. In the meantime, could I leave the water to you? It's rather tricky to draw it with our talons...

84.original: To the northwest of here, you will find a stream fed by a cascade. Its water runs cool and clear and should serve your needs. Here, this should help you to carry the items.

85.original: Right, let's get to work. After you have the water, please come and meet me in the fields in Voeburtenburg.

86.original: You draw a bottle of pristine water and store it inside the worn sack.

87.original: There you are. Did you get the water?

88.original: Great! I'll put the clay with it in the sack.

89.original: That leaves us with only the fae lamp, which I understand is with the pixies.
